subject: AWS Marketplace listing — usage visibility, territory language & co-sell plan
messages:
From: Rebecca Li <rebecca.li@acme-corp.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: aws-marketplace-seller-support@amazon.com
Date: 2026-08-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: AWS listing questions — usage visibility / territories / co-sell alignment

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We are finalizing the assets for our marketplace listing and have a couple items that will affect procurement and our internal legal review. Quick list below — can you confirm how Redwood plans to signal these in the public product page and in the private offer flow?

1) Usage visibility: our finance team needs to know what usage metrics Redwood will make available to the buyer (monthly spend, seats/instances, token counts, or only AMI/instance consumption?). We attached a screen grab of the dashboard we expect (2026-08-19_acme_usage_dashboard.png).

2) Territory / licensing language: we sell to multiple global subsidiaries. Does your listing need per-region SKU language, or can we include a single global entitlement clause? Any recommended text is helpful.

3) Co-sell contact & opt-in: procurement wants a short blurb on the product page that explains the co-sell offer (sales enablement, deal registration, and who the buyer contacts). Is that part of the public listing copy or handled in the co-sell playbook post-purchase?

4) Pricing footnote: we will offer a 6-month trial credit in our private offer. Want to ensure the footnote language complies with AWS marketplace rules.

Can your team share drafted copy for the product page and a short checklist for what needs to be in the private offer description? If easier, we can jump on a 30-minute sync later today.

Thanks — Rebecca

--
Rebecca Li

Subject: Re: AWS listing questions — usage visibility / territories / co-sell alignment

Hi Rebecca — thanks for the clear list and the dashboard screenshot, helpful context. Quick answers below; I also attached our current draft of the product page copy (aws-listing-draft-copy-v3.md) so you can see where we're proposing each element.

1) Usage visibility
- Public product page: we include high-level billing model (usage-based, token-equivalent units) and an estimated cost calc for sample workloads. We do not publish per-customer token counts publicly.
- Post-purchase / Marketplace metering: AWS Marketplace supports buyer-level metering reports (monthly usage and spend) which we can enable — those reports are accessible to the buyer and shared via the AWS billing pipeline. For procurement, we can also provide a CSV export hook on request (subject to an NDA for aggregated customer reports).

2) Territory / licensing language
- Recommendation: use a single entitlement clause on the public page that says "Global commercial use; engagement and support scope may vary by region." For private offers, we include explicit territory rows (list of countries) and per-subsidiary SKUs if the buyer requests localized billing.
- I'll draft two short alternatives (global vs. regional) below and Vanessa can pick voice: 
  • Global-friendly: "Available for commercial use worldwide. For local billing and deployment requirements, contact sales to request region-specific entitlements."
  • Region-specific (short): "Available in: United States, Canada, EU (all member states), UK, Australia, Japan, Singapore. For other territories contact sales."

3) Co-sell contact & opt-in
- Best practice: include a one-line public blurb on the product page (for discovery) that points buyers to a co-sell eligibility email/portal (we can provide a link). The detailed co-sell onboarding lives off-page (private playbook) — we will coordinate post-purchase.
- Proposed one-liner for the product page: "Co-sell eligible — contact our channel team to explore joint GTM and deal registration."

4) Pricing footnote
- Trial credits and private offer credits should be reflected in the private offer description and the footnote should say: "Promotional credits expire 6 months from issuance; see private offer terms for eligibility." We cannot put conditional promotional mechanics on the public listing beyond a simple note. AWS seller support typically wants that phrasing; we've passed similar language in other Listings.

Next steps
- Vanessa: can you review the tone on the two territory wording options and the one-liner for co-sell?
- I'll update the draft copy and push to the Drive link in this thread.

Happy to do a quick call — I have 2:30–3:30pm PT open today.

Best,
Mateo

--

Subject: Re: AWS listing questions — usage visibility / territories / co-sell alignment

Thanks for the draft, Mateo — I made a few tone and compliance-oriented edits inline in the attached md (aws-listing-draft-copy-v3.md). Main suggestions below for Rebecca to consider:

- Territory language: prefer the global-friendly option as default on the public page; add a small expandable section titled "Regional availability" that lists supported regions for discoverability without implying legal commitments.
- Co-sell blurb: tighten to one short sentence and add a link to the co-sell form: "Co-sell eligible — register your opportunity here: https://partners.redwood.ai/register"
- Usage visibility: call out clearly on the product page that buyers will have access to monthly usage and spend reports via AWS billing, and that any custom exports require a written request.
- Pricing footnote: add the phrase "contact sales to redeem trial credits" to prevent support tickets from buyers.

I also included a short checklist (end of the doc) for private-offer fields AWS expects: private description, supply account id, offer end date, promotional credit clause, territory list, and co-sell eligibility flag.

Rebecca — if that matches your expectations I can fold these edits into the final copy and we can run through AWS seller support validation tomorrow morning.

—Vanessa
